blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Evaluation of Computer-Use Agents (CUAs) is often limited to the final deliverables they create (at the end of hundreds of steps) and assessed with functional verifiers, as seen in OSWorld. However, such evaluation of end-state performance lacks transparency into how and why agents fail in various tasks, obfuscating critical insight for subsequent improvement. For instance, agents that err during keyboard inputs would require a different mitigation strategy from those that fail to precisely provide click-based inputs on the graphical UI. We introduce OSWorld-Pro: a set of over 300 tasks containing over 2800 subgoals to enable the procedural evaluation of CUAs grounded in over 67,000 human annotations. We use robust human-aligned LLM-Judges to evaluate the fulfillment of OSWorld-Pro subgoals and thereby reveal the progress that models make throughout a series of sequentially dependent subgoals. Our findings reveal that OSWorld-Pro is challenging even for state-of-the-art LLMs, with top performers like Claude Opus 5 achieving only 75.7% vs. 83.4% on OSWorld. Furthermore, we identify critical process-focused failure modes of various models (e.g. subgoal-irrelevant actions and click-based mistakes) to provide insights to improve performance and efficiency of CUAs.
blocks.zh: 对计算机使用代理(CUAs)的评价往往局限于它们创造的最终可达到的目标(以数百个步骤结束),并用功能验证器进行评估,这在OSWorld中就可以看到了. 然而,对结束状态业绩的这种评价缺乏透明度,无法了解代理人如何和为什么在各种任务中失败,从而模糊了以后改进的重要见解。 例如,在键盘输入过程中出错的代理商需要不同的缓解策略,而不是那些未能在图形用户界面上提供精确点击输入的代理商. 我们提出OSWorld-Pro:一套300多项任务,其中包括2 800多个次级目标,以便能够在67 000多篇人文说明的基础上对海关协调理事会进行程序评价。 我们利用与人类一致的LLM法官来评价OSWorld-Pro次级目标的实现情况,从而揭示模式在一系列依次依赖的次级目标方面取得的进展。 我们的发现显示,OSWorld-Pro甚至对最先进的LLMS也具有挑战性,克洛德·奥普斯5等顶尖表演者在OSWorld上只取得了75.7%对83.4%的成绩. 此外,我们查明各种模式(如次级目标相关行动和以点击为基础的错误)的关键的以进程为重点的失败模式,以提供见解,提高统一协议的绩效和效率。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Humans use computers to tackle long-horizon tasks involving many interdependent subgoals, tracking their progress through intermediate milestones rather than relying solely on final outcomes. For example, in a machine learning research project such as the one presented in this paper, researchers assess progress by monitoring data collection, iterating on computational experiments, and visualizing experimental results. In such situations, humans often do not rely on final outcomes alone (such as completed paper manuscripts) and instead utilize the status of various constituent subgoals to determine how these projects are progressing. Using the same vein of thought, we believe that process-based evaluations of Computer-Use Agents can complement existing benchmarks based on outcome-based evaluations (e.g. OSWorld).
blocks.zh: 人类利用计算机来处理涉及许多相互依存的分目标的长期任务,通过中间里程碑跟踪其进展,而不是仅仅依靠最终结果。 例如,在本文所介绍的机器学习研究项目中,研究人员通过监测数据收集、反复进行计算实验以及可视化实验结果来评估进展。 在这种情况下,人类往往不单单依靠最终结果(如已完成的纸稿),而是利用各种构成次级目标的地位来确定这些项目的进展情况。 利用同样的思路,我们认为,基于过程的计算机使用代理人评价可以补充基于成果评价(如OSWorld)的现有基准.

blocks.en: Outcome-based evaluations were utilized with great success on math capabilities in terms of GSM8K ( Cobbe et al., 2021 ) and AIME 25 ( White et al., 2025 ) and later in coding environments (using unit tests) such as LiveCodeBench ( Jain et al., 2024 ) as well as scientific question answering in GPQA ( Rein et al., 2023 ) , MMLU-Pro ( Wang et al., 2024 ) , and HLE ( Phan et al., 2025 ) . Outcome-based evaluation was also applied on CUA capabilities in works such as the widely-adopted OSWorld ( Xie et al., 2024 ) and OSUniverse ( Davydova et al., 2025 ) . These works construct functional verifiers against the final deliverables of the tasks and measure the success of agents based on whether the deliverables match various aspects of reference files. Beyond desktop GUI agents, there have also been adjacent work relating to Android GUI ( Rawles et al., 2025 ) as well as tool calling ability with model context protocol ( Jia et al., 2025 ) .
blocks.zh: 根据GSM8K(Cobbe等人,2021年)和AIME 25(White等人,2025年),以及后来的编码环境(使用单位测试),如LiveCode Bench(Jain等人,2024年),以及GPQA(Rein等人,2023年),MMLU-Pro(Wang等人,2024年)和HLE(Phan等人,2025年)的科学问题回答,对数学能力进行了非常成功的利用。 在广泛采用的OSWorld(Xie等,2024年)和OSUniverse(Davydova等,2025年)等作品中,对CUA能力也进行了成果评价。 这些工作对照任务的最终交付成果构建了功能核查器,并根据交付成果是否与参考文件的各个方面相匹配来衡量代理人的成功。 除了桌面GUI代理外,还有与Android GUI有关的相邻工作(Rawles等,2025年)以及用模型上下文协议调用能力的工具(Jia等,2025年)。

blocks.en:
However, such outcome-based evaluation approaches for CUAs have some limitations. First, they are unable to discriminate between trajectories with different progression in tasks that have yet to create final deliverables. For instance, in Fig. 1 , final deliverables will not be available whether the agent fails at the first subgoal or the ninth subgoal and hence the agent will receive a zero for both trajectories even though the agent has progressed much further in the later trajectory. Such poor discernibility becomes more critical in long-horizon tasks (e.g. requiring hundreds of steps and therefore have a high likelihood of failure prior to final deliverable creation).
Second, as CUAs become stronger, they will also be more capable in terms of reward hacking, which means that these agents can get to the correct final outcome through undesirable ways. The recent OpenAI security incident ( OpenAI, 2026a ) highlights how strong agents can literally hack third-party servers to obtain restricted information (i.e. answer keys) in order to do well on outcome-based evaluations.
Finally, outcome-based evaluations do not provided fine-grained information on the contribution of individual steps within the agent trajectory, which can be useful to assess how efficiently agents advance on long-horizon tasks. Process-based evaluation addresses these limitations by focusing not only on what final outcomes CUAs arrive at but also how they get there.
blocks.zh:
然而,对海关协调会的这种基于成果的评价方法有一些局限性。 首先,它们无法区分在尚未产生最终成果的任务中进度不同的轨迹。 例如,在图一中,不管代理人在第一个次级目标或第九个次级目标上失败,都无法获得最后交付品,因此,即使代理人在以后的轨道上取得了更进一步的进展,该代理人将获得两个轨道的零。 这种不易察觉性在长期任务中变得更加重要(例如,需要数百个步骤,因此在最终交付品创造之前很有可能失败)。
第二,随着CUA的加强,它们也会在奖励黑客方面更有能力,这意味着这些特工可以通过不可取的方式获得正确的最终结果. 近期的OpenAI安全事件(OpenAI,2026a)凸显出强力特工可以如何从字面上黑入第三方服务器以获取受限制的信息(即接应键),以便在基于结果的评价上做得好.
最后,基于成果的评价没有提供关于个体步骤在物剂轨迹中的贡献的精细信息,这可能有助于评估物剂如何高效地推进长期任务。 以进程为基础的评价不仅侧重于统一审计准则的最终成果,而且侧重于这些成果如何实现。

blocks.en: To design process-based evaluation for CUAs, we draw inspiration from PRM-800k ( Lightman et al., 2023 ) and ProcessBench ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) , which are process-based evaluations for math capabilities. Specifically, these benchmarks break down reasoning on solving math problems into distinct steps. Then, they seek to identify where errors first occur in the reasoning chain. CUA tasks tend to be much more open-ended compared to math tasks in PRM-800K and ProcessBench, as CUA tasks often have multiple approaches to reach the required goal. Therefore, we adapt ideas from works on rubrics ( Gunjal et al., 2025 ; Arora et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2026 ) . Specifically, we break down the overarching task goal into subgoals that can be individually assessed for completion. However, unlike rubrics, which are typically requirements that models can fulfill independently, subgoals in many CUA tasks are dependent on each other. This means that an earlier subgoal has to be completed before moving to the next subgoal.
blocks.zh: 为了设计CUA的以过程为基础的评价,我们从PRM-800k(Lightman等,2023年)和Process Bench(Zheng等,2025年)中汲取灵感,它们是数学能力的以过程为基础的评价. 具体而言,这些基准将解决数学问题的推理细分为不同的步骤。 然后,它们寻求识别推理链中首先出错的地方. 与PRM-800K和Process Bench中的数学任务相比,CUA任务往往更加开放,因为CUA任务往往有多种方法来实现需要的目标. 因此,我们从关于标题的作品(Gunjal等,2025;Arora等,2025;Wang等,2026)中修改想法。 具体地说,我们把总的任务目标细分为可单独评估完成的次级目标。 然而,与通常要求模型能够独立实现的Rumics不同,许多CUA任务中的子目标彼此依赖. 这意味着在转向下一个次级目标之前,必须完成较早的次级目标。

blocks.en: To support process-based evaluation for CUAs, we present OSWorld-Pro: a benchmark with over 67, 000 step-level human annotations across more than 2800 progressive subgoals in over 300 long-horizon CUA tasks. The main features for OSWorld-Pro are:
blocks.zh: 为支持CUA的流程评价,我们提出OSWorld-Pro:一个基准,在300多项长期CUA任务的2800多个进步次级目标中,有67 000多分层次的人类说明。 OSWorld-Pro的主要功能为:

blocks.en: 1. Long-Horizon : Tasks have an average of 9.2 sequentially dependent subgoals per task, for which earlier subgoals have to be completed prior to attempt subsequent ones. This is in contrary to benchmarks like OSWorld where tasks mostly have a single subgoal (see example in Fig 2 ) and ChainWorld ( Siu et al., 2026 ) , which chains up multiple loosely-connected OSWorld tasks and do not reflect the interdependent nature of subgoals in real-world long-horizon tasks.
blocks.zh: 1. 联合国 长相: 每个任务平均有9.2个依次依次依赖的次级目标,在尝试后续目标之前必须完成较早的次级目标。 这与OSWorld等基准背道而驰,OSWorld的任务大多有一个单一的分目标(见图2的例子)和ChainWorld(Siu等,2026年),它们将多个松散相联的OSWorld的任务连在一起,并不反映分目标在现实世界长视野任务中的相互依存性质.

blocks.en: 2. Challenging : Tasks require an average of 3.45 unique apps to complete, which is substantially more compared to OSWorld at 1.34. In addition, we include rare apps such as Videos, Archive Manager and LibreOffice Draw and uncommon Linux and GUI distributions - beyond Ubuntu with GNOME - (e.g. AlmaLinux and MATE) not found in OSWorld to test generalization capabilities. Among top performing models, Claude Opus 5 only reaches 75.7% vs. 83.4% on OSWorld ( XLANG-Lab, 2025 ) .
blocks.zh: 2. 挑战:任务平均需要3.45个独特的应用软件才能完成,比OSWorld的1.34要多得多。 此外,我们还包括了视频,存档管理器和LibreOffice Draw等罕见的应用软件以及不寻常的Linux和GUI发行——在Ubuntu之外还有GNOME——(如AlmaLinux和MATE)在OSWorld没有用于测试通缩能力. 在顶级表现模式中,克洛德·奥普斯5号在OSWorld上只达到75.7%对83.4%(XLANG-Lab,2025.

blocks.en: 3. Fine-grained : Beyond providing an aggregate metric that shows how well an agent performs, OSWorld-Pro allows users to understand the type of actions that it commonly fails on, how efficient it is in completing subgoals over its trajectories and how it react when facing infeasible subgoals, as common in real-world tasks. For instance, Claude Opus 5 was shown to occasionally engage in subgoal-irrelevant actions (sometimes for over 50-steps) despite completing all subgoals.
blocks.zh: 3个 精细的: OSWorld-Pro除了提供一个显示代理业绩的汇总度量表之外,还允许用户了解它通常失败的行动类型、它在完成次级目标方面对其轨迹的效率如何,以及面对现实世界中常见的不可行的次级目标时如何作出反应。 例如,Claude Opus 5被证明偶尔参与与次级目标有关的行动(有时超过50步),尽管完成了所有次级目标。

blocks.en: 2 OSWorld-Pro Overview
blocks.zh: OS World-Pro 概览

blocks.en: OSWorld-Pro contains 67,264 human-annotated labels across 305 distinct tasks with 2814 progressive subgoals. These tasks span three categories: Diversity (117 tasks), covering less commonly benchmarked applications; Coordination (109 tasks), requiring coordination across ≥ 4 \geq 4 applications; and Robustness (79 tasks), testing generalization across Linux distributions and graphical interfaces. Specifically, samples contains agent trajectories on various tasks as well as step-level human annotations on how each step targets various subgoals, determine their feasibility and monitor their progression and final completion. While the sheer number of tasks (305) is comparable to the 369 tasks in OSWorld ( Xie et al., 2024 ) and 160 tasks in OSUniverse ( Davydova et al., 2025 ) , each OSWorld-Pro task has 2 orders of magnitude more granular human-annotated verification signals (collected over > 5000 >5000 person-hours) compared to alternatives. We show an example in Fig. 2 , a visualization of data distribution in Fig. 3 , and further descriptive statistics in § B .
blocks.zh: OSWorld-Pro包含67,264个人类附加标签,涵盖305个不同的任务,并有2814个进步分目标. 这些任务分为三类:多样性(117个任务),涵盖基准化程度较低的应用;协调(109个任务),需要协调QQ 4\geq 4应用;和强力(79个任务),测试Linux分布和图形界面的通缩. 具体地说,样本中包含各种任务的物剂轨迹,以及关于每个步骤如何针对各种次级目标、确定其可行性并监测其进展和最终完成情况的分级人类说明。 虽然任务数量之多(305个)与OSWorld的369个任务(Xie等人,2024年)和OSUniverse的160个任务(Davydova等人,2025年)相当,但每个OSWorld-Pro任务拥有两个数量级的更颗粒的人类附加核查信号(收集量大于5000个 > 5000个人小时),而替代品则不同. 我们以图2为例,以图3为数据分布的可视化,以第B节为例,进一步说明性统计数字。

blocks.en: 3 Data Collection
blocks.zh: 3个 数据收集

blocks.en: To ensure annotation quality, we select qualified annotators through screening, training and pairing each annotator with an experienced reviewer. Annotators with Bachelors’ degrees or higher, as well as ≥ 6 \geq 6 months of experience working on Computer-Use Agent annotation are recruited and managed by our vendor. Prior to their inclusion into the project, we check that they pass tests on English capabilities, Linux proficiency (post mandatory training) and understanding of the annotation workflow (through two sample tasks reviewed against golden references). Each annotator works through the entire agent trajectory of a task and is supported by a reviewer (with substantial annotation experience) to iteratively review the annotator’s work and to provide feedback for improvement where helpful. Across 305 tasks, 25 annotators and reviewers from 5 countries were involved. Further details on annotator recruitment in § C .
blocks.zh: 为了确保注释的质量,我们通过筛选、培训和将每个注释员与有经验的审查员配对,挑选合格的注释员。 拥有学士学位或以上学位的注释员,以及6-eq6个月从事计算机使用代理注释工作的经验由我们的供应商招聘和管理。 在他们被纳入项目之前,我们检查他们是否通过英语能力测试,Linux熟练程度测试(后必修训练)以及对注释工作流程的理解(通过两个对照黄金参考书审查的样本任务). 每个注释员通过任务的整个代理轨迹工作,并得到一名审查员(具有大量注释经验)的支持,以便反复地审查注释员的工作,并在有帮助的情况下提供改进的反馈。 在305项任务中,有5个国家的25名注释员和审查员参与。 关于第C节中说明人招聘的进一步详情。

blocks.en:
We generate tasks using the approach described in ProCUA-SFT ( Jung et al., 2026 ) for human annotation.
Specifically, for the Diversity category, we identify tasks containing applications that are underrepresented in existing computer-use benchmarks (e.g. Videos, Archive Manager and LibreOffice Draw).
For the Coordination category, we select tasks that require coordinated use of at least four applications. By comparison, tasks in OSWorld involve at most four applications.
For the Robustness category, we generate additional tasks using the ProCUA-SFT approach 1 1 1 We use Kimi-K2.6, available in May 2026, instead of Kimi-K2.5. in environments that differ from the default Ubuntu/GNOME setup. These environments include Linux distributions such as Fedora, Alpine, and AlmaLinux, and graphical interfaces such as bspwm, Xfce, and LXQt, as detailed in Fig. 3 . These tasks evaluate how well models generalize across Linux distributions and graphical interfaces.
blocks.zh:
我们使用ProCUA-SFT(Jung等人,2026年)中描述的人类注释方法生成任务。
具体地说,对于多样性类别,我们确定了包含在现有计算机使用基准中代表性不足的应用程序的任务(如视频、档案管理器和LibreOffice Draw)。

blocks.en: Our annotation workflow consists of task validation, annotator assignment, step-level labeling, and lastly independent and interactive review. (1) Task validation Prior to human annotations, our vendor inspects and removes tasks that have unclear or under-specified goals or have safety concerns. In addition, the subgoals and application required by each subgoal are also manually inspected and corrected where appropriate. In addition, we skip tasks where subgoals are not sequentially dependent on one another (i.e. only include tasks where earlier subgoals need to be completed before later subgoals). In doing so, we avoid overly simple tasks with multiple unrelated subgoals (e.g. open a video file, then open an unrelated text document) to focus on long-horizon tasks that are more challenging and realistic. (2) Annotator assignment We assign tasks to technical or non-technical annotator pools based on the applications and skills involved. Tasks requiring coding knowledge, such as those involving coding in VS Code or the terminal, are assigned to technical annotators. (3) Step-level labeling Annotators label each step of pre-generated model trajectories to identify the subgoal(s) 2 2 2 This is almost always a single subgoal but < < 2% of steps do effectively target two or more subgoals. that a step targets. In some environments, we notice that the targeted subgoal is not feasible. For example, a subgoal may require selecting an option from the file menu that does not exist. Therefore, we also ask annotators to indicate whether the targeted subgoal(s) are feasible. Following OSWorld ( Xie et al., 2024 ) , we keep tasks with infeasible subgoals in order to understand what models would do in similar real-world tasks. If it is feasible, annotators also indicate if the current step makes progress on and completes the subgoal. (4) Independent and interactive review Inspired by the annotation workflow in ProfBench ( Wang et al., 2026 ) , our workflow involves having a reviewer to iteratively provide feedback for the annotator to modify their annotations. However, because the task is time-consuming (annotators spend between 5 to 20 hours per task depending on the number of steps taken), we found it challenging for reviewers to provide comprehensive feedback, despite their strength in precisely pointing out inadequacies. Therefore, we modify our workflow based on the approach taken in HelpSteer3 ( Wang et al., 2025b ) such that the reviewer has to first independently annotate the task before providing feedback to the annotator with the annotation platform (Super Annotate) highlighting the differences in initial annotations. Annotators were not allowed to use LLMs during the annotation task, with extensive checks to ensure compliance (e.g. based on repetition patterns and annotation durations). Full annotation guidelines are in § D .

blocks.en: 4 Can LLMs effectively judge like humans do?
blocks.zh: 4 LLMS能像人类那样有效判断吗?

blocks.en: Given the high cost of having humans evaluate agent trajectories, many works ( Starace et al., 2025 ; Arora et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2026 ) have turned to using LLM-Judges to proxy human judgments. Computer Use Agent trajectories are particularly challenging to evaluate because they are path-dependent across long-horizons (e.g. across hundreds of steps) while evaluation of agent outputs (e.g. in OSWorld) is only state-dependent, without considering how the agent arrived at the final state. More precisely, the role of the LLM Judge is to identify which subgoal(s) are targeted by every step of the agent trajectory, whether that subgoal is feasible at the step and if so, whether the agent makes progress and/or completes the subgoal at that step.
blocks.zh: 鉴于人类评价物剂轨迹的成本很高,许多作品(Starace等人,2025年;Arora等人,2025年;Wang等人,2026年)转而使用LLM-法官代理人类判决. 计算机 使用Agent轨迹对评价特别有挑战性,因为它们跨长视线(例如跨越数百个步骤)依赖路径,而Agent输出的评价(例如OSWorld)只依赖状态,而不考虑Agent如何到达最终状态. 更确切地说,LLM法官的作用是确定代理轨迹的每一步骤都针对哪些次级目标,该次级目标在该步骤是否可行,如果可行,该代理人在该步骤是否取得进展并(或)完成该次级目标。

blocks.en: 4.1 Evaluation
blocks.zh: 4.1 评价

blocks.en: To evaluate LLM-Judges, we use Macro-F1 based on the human-labeled ground-truth and the model-predicted label as used by ProfBench ( Wang et al., 2026 ) and PaperBench ( Starace et al., 2025 ) . Subgoal(s) targeted is first binarized into whether each subgoal is targeted by a particular step while the other fields (feasibility, progression and completion) are innately binary. Given the dependent nature of the fields, we consider values in fields iff the pre-requisite field was correct. This means we consider feasibility iff the correct set of subgoals were identified, progression iff feasibility was correct and completion iff progression was correct.
blocks.zh: 为了评价LLM-法官,我们使用Macro-F1,其基础是人类标记的地面真象和Bench教授(王等,2026年)和Paper Bench(Starace等,2025年)所用的模型预想标签。 鉴于字段的依赖性,如果事先要求的字段是正确的,我们认为字段的价值是正确的。 这意味着,如果确定了正确的一套次级目标,那么我们认为可行性;如果进展的可行性是正确的,那么完成的可行性是正确的。

blocks.en:
We ran early experiments with GPT-5.6-Luna (with default medium reasoning), a lightweight, affordable and feasible at high concurrency. The complexity of judgment task (with hundreds of step over tens of subgoals) required extensive explorations in LLM-judge design, which we discuss in § F .
Our final design involves evaluating an entire trajectory in a single API request. Because this requires sending a payload of up to hundreds of screenshots in a single request (requiring 500 MBs), we only found success in using OpenAI GPT-5.6 models while others (e.g. Claude, Gemini and Open Models) raised various errors relating to payload size, image quantity or context window. Cost estimation method is detailed in § G .
blocks.zh:
我们用GPT-5.6-Luna(带有默认的中度推理)进行了早期的实验,一种轻量级,可负担的和可操作的高通币. 判断任务的复杂性(与数十个次级目标相比有数百个步骤)要求对LLM法官的设计进行广泛的探索,我们在F节中对此进行了讨论。
我们的最终设计涉及在一个API请求中评估整个轨迹. 由于这需要在一次请求中发送多达数百个截图的有效载荷(需要500个MB),我们只发现成功使用OpenAI GPT-5.6型号,而其他(如克洛德,双子座和开放型号)则提出了与有效载荷大小,图像数量或上下文窗口有关的各种错误. 成本估算方法详见§G.

blocks.en: In addition to Macro-F1 at the step level, we want to understand how well the LLM-Judge can predict human annotations at three complementary levels. First at the step level, we calculate a simple mean across macro-F1 across subgoal {targeted, feasibility, progression, completion}. Next at the subgoal level, we tabulate the proportion of subgoals that have their final completion status across all steps in a trajectory predicted correctly. Subgoals are considered completed iff at least one step has the targeted subgoal labeled as completed. Finally, at the task level, we calculate an overage task performance based on the percentage of subgoals completed. We calculate a mean absolute error (MAE) between the human-annotated and model-predicted performance and take the average across all tasks. Finally, we calculate 1-MAE to make the metric higher as better and improve readability.
blocks.zh: 除了一步级的Macro-F1外,我们想了解LLM-法官在三个互补层面如何能很好地预测人的说明. 首先,在步骤一级,我们在次级目标{目标、可行性、进展、完成}的宏观-F1之间计算一个简单的平均值。 其次,在次级目标一级,我们按正确预测的轨迹,列出所有步骤最终完成的次级目标的比例。 如果目标次级目标至少有一步被标为已完成,则该次级目标被视为已完成。 最后,在任务一级,我们根据次级目标完成的百分比计算超额任务业绩。 我们计算人类附加说明和模型预测的性能之间的一个平均绝对错误(MAE),并在所有任务中取平均值. 最后,我们计算出1-MAE,使度量值提高,提高可读性。

blocks.en: To understand how reliable the Annotators’ labels are, we compare them to the Reviewer’s initial annotations prior to see annotations from the Annotator and providing feedback to the Annotator. This provide a measure of how much two independent annotators would agree. We find excellent agreement (Cohen’s κ \kappa > > 0.8) across all aspects with 0.987 for subgoal targeted, 0.847 for feasibility, 0.869 for progression and 0.940 for completion.

blocks.en: The top performing model GPT-5.6-Sol with max reasoning effort approaches Human Performance on identifying targeted subgoals (97.0 vs 98.4%) and comes close on predicting subgoal completion at the step, subgoal and task levels (within 3.3% absolute different from humans) as shown in Tab. 1 . However, it substantially lags behind on predicting subgoal feasibility (61.9 vs. 91.6%) and progress (74.7 vs. 94.1%), which also have lower agreement rates between independent human annotators (Cohen’s κ \kappa =0.847-0.869 vs 0.940-0.987). We suspect it is because these fields are more subjective as it might not always be clear whether a task is infeasible or a practical method to achieve a goal has not yet been found. For example, when locating an option under a menu with various unexpanded sub-menus, a feasible subgoal might appear infeasible until the menu option is discovered (or vice-versa). Similarly, whether a step meaningfully helps to progress toward a subgoal might at times be ambiguous. For instance, if a step modifies a piece of code to add a new functionality but results in a bug, a judge can reasonably justify both progress=No or progress=Yes depending on what the focus is on.
blocks.zh: 业绩最好的GPT-5.6-Sol模型,最大推理努力,将人类绩效用于确定目标分目标(97.0对98.4%),并接近于预测分目标分目标完成情况,如Tab所示(在绝对与人类相差3.3%)。 1 然而,在预测次级目标可行性(61.9对91.6%)和进展(74.7对94.1%)方面远远落后,后者的独立人名注释者之间的协议率也较低。 (Cohen的\kappa = 0.847-0.869对0.940-0.987). 我们怀疑这是因为这些领域比较主观,因为可能并不总是清楚一项任务是否不可行,或者是否尚未找到实现目标的实际方法。 例如,在菜单下找到一个带有各种未扩展子菜单的选项时,一个可行的子目标可能会显得不可行,直到菜单选项被发现(或者反之亦然). 同样,一个步骤是否有意义地有助于朝着次级目标取得进展,有时可能是模棱两可的。 例如,如果一个步骤修改了一个代码以添加一个新的功能,但导致一个错误,法官可以合理地证明两个进步= 无或进展= 是的,取决于焦点是什么。

blocks.en: Within the GPT-5.6 model family, larger models generally do better than smaller models but the improvement plateaus. For instance, the step level performance (Mean of 4 Macro-F1s) in Tab. 1 substantially increase from 75.7 (Luna) to 80.9 (Terra) and then only slightly increases to 82.0 (Sol) while at Max reasoning. This rate of increase is roughly inline with gains in total cost, which first increases 10x and then rises only 1.6x. When constrained on API cost, increasing the reasoning effort on a smaller model often beats a lower reasoning effort on a larger model at a lower cost. For instance, GPT-5.6-Terra Max slightly outperforms GPT-5.6-Sol Medium at 22% lower price while GPT-5.6-Luna Max generally matches GPT-5.6-Terra Low at one-sixth cost.
blocks.zh: 在GPT-5.6模型家族中,较大的模型一般比较小的模型但改进高地做得更好. 例如,在Tab. 1中,步级性能(指4 Macro-F1s)从75.7(Luna)大幅增加到80.9(Terra),然后在Max推理中只略微增至82.0(Sol)。 这种增速与总成本的增益大致一致,首先增加10x,后只增加1.6x. 当受API成本所限制时,在更小的模型上加大推理努力往往会以更低的成本在更大的模型上击败更低的推理努力. 例如,GPT-5.6-Terra Max以22%的价格略高于GPT-5.6-Sol Medium,而GPT-5.6-Luna Max一般与GPT-5.6-Terra相匹配。 低价的六分之一成本。

blocks.en: Models generally perform better at higher reasoning efforts across most metrics. However, there are two major exceptions to the rule. Models sometimes perform better with no reasoning compared to low reasoning. This might be because given models insufficient thinking tokens might artificially cut short its explicit thinking process, while non-reasoning model are unaffected in their implicit, latent reasoning through hidden layers ( Li et al., 2025 ) . Subgoal Feasibility performance generally also lowers with higher reasoning effort (on Terra and Sol). Such a correlation is also observed in terms of the likelihood for models to predict feasibility=No. The proportion of feasibility=No decreases from 9.7% at GPT-5.6-Sol None to 5.1% at GPT-5.6-Sol Max while human-annotated ground-truth is at 15.3%. This suggests that increased reasoning effort results in models over-estimating the feasibility of tasks and hence resulting in lower macro-F1.
blocks.zh: 模型一般在大多数衡量标准的更高推理努力中表现更好。 然而,该规则有两大例外. 与低推理相比,模型有时在没有推理的情况下表现得更好. 这可能是因为给定模型的思考符号不足可能会人为地缩短其明确的思考过程,而非理性模型则通过隐藏层而不受其隐含和潜在推理的影响(Li等,2025年)。 次级目标的可行性业绩一般也随着(关于Terra和Sol)的推理努力而降低。 在模型预测可行性的可能性方面也观察到这种相关性= 可行性比例=无,从GPT-5.6-Sol None的9.7%下降到了GPT-5.6-Sol Max的5.1%,而人为说明的地面实况为15.3%。 这表明,加大推理努力导致模型高估任务可行性,从而降低宏观F1。

blocks.en: Following Xie et al. (2024) and Jung et al. (2026) , we formalize the task as given a goal alongside an computer-use Linux environment with Graphical UI (that it can ”see” via screenshots), the agent (VLM with harness defined in OSWorld) should generate a trajectory that addresses the goal. Subsequently, we use the best-performing GPT-5.6-Sol Max judge from § 4 to evaluate whether steps fulfill various subgoals. Finally, we report the percentage of tasks across each category that complete all subgoals deemed feasible by human annotators. We believe that GPT-5.6-Sol Max judge is an adequate proxy of human judgments as it matches human judgment in 94.1%, closely trailing independent reviewers at 95.6% from Tab. 1 . In addition, GPT-5.6-Sol Max scores itself lower than 4 other models, alleviating our initial concerns over potential self-preference bias. Our evaluation setup largely follows OSWorld GitHub ( XLANG-Lab, 2024 ) and evaluates only vision-language models with publicly available harnesses there (detailed in § G ).

blocks.en: Overall, Claude Opus 4.8 with Max effort achieves the best performance in Tab. 2 at 77.7% Overall, which means that OSWorld-Pro is substantially more challenging than OSWorld where the top Opus model scores 83.4% ( XLANG-Lab, 2025 ) . OSWorld-Pro is particularly challenging for open-weight models with the top model only achieving 55.1% whereas open-weight models scores > > 80% on OSWorld. For a matched model, Minimax M3 scores only 28.9% on OSWorld-Pro but 75.2% on OSWorld. This indicates that OSWorld-Pro can be a good target for open-weight models to hill-climb against, without being saturated or overly-difficult such that improvements are hard to achieve.
blocks.zh: 总体来说,克洛德·奥普斯4.8与马克斯的努力在Tab. 2中以77.7%的总成绩取得最佳成绩,这意味着OSWorld-Pro比OSWorld更具挑战性,而OSWorld的顶级奥普斯模型得分83.4%(XLANG-Lab,2025年). OSWorld-Pro对于开放量级模型尤其具有挑战性,顶级模型只达到55.1%,而开放量级模型在OSWorld上得分 > 80%. 对于匹配的模型,Minimax M3在OSWorld-Pro上只得28.9%分,而OSWorld上则得75.2%分. 这表明OSWorld-Pro可以成为开放量级模型对接山地攀登的好目标,而不会饱和或过于困难以致难以实现改进.

blocks.en: Among open-weight models, scores are generally highest on the Diversity category (least challenging), followed by Coordination and finally Robustness (most challenging). This means that open-weight models generalize best to rare applications, moderately to longer-horizon workflows requiring coordination between ≥ 4 \geq 4 apps and worst on different Linux distributions and graphical interfaces. One possible explanation for the poor performance relating to generalizations across different Linux and graphical UI environment is the general lack of such data within training environments, due to the limited commercial advantage of improving on them (given how esoteric they are in real-world work settings). Therefore, models are forced to generalize out-of-distribution from Ubuntu/GNOME environments that are more common in training data ( Wang et al., 2025a ; Jung et al., 2026 ) .
blocks.zh: 在开放量级模型中,多样性类的分数一般最高(挑战性最小),其次是"协调",最后是"强健"(挑战性最强). 这意味着开放量级模型对稀有应用进行最普遍的概括,对需要QQ 4\geq 4应用之间协调的中度到更长范围的工作流程,对不同的Linux发行和图形界面最坏. 不同Linux和图形化UI环境中的通用性差的一个可能解释是,培训环境中普遍缺乏这类数据,因为改善这类数据的商业优势有限(考虑到在现实世界的工作环境中,这些数据是何等的)。 因此,模型被迫从Ubuntu/GNOME环境中概括出在培训数据中更为常见的分布(Wang等,2025a;Jung等,2026).

blocks.en: To understand the role that model-size plays on OSWorld-Pro performance, we conduct some analysis across both closed-source and open-weight models. Closed-source models in general perform better compared to open-weights one. As the parameter counts for closed models are not publicly reported, we use the observation that within the same model family, more expensive models by API pricing are likely to be larger (e.g. GPT-5.6 Sol > > Terra > > Luna, Opus 5 > > Sonnet 5). We find no obvious evidence that larger parameter count alone translates to better performance on OSWorld-Pro given that Sonnet 5 does better than Opus 5 (but worse than Opus 4.7 and 4.8) and GPT-5.6 Luna does better than Terra but worse than Sol.
blocks.zh: 为了了解模型大小对OSWorld-Pro性能的作用,我们对闭源模型和开量模型进行一些分析. 与开口量一相比,闭源模型一般表现较好. 由于封闭模型的参数计数没有公开报告,我们使用一种观察,即在同一模型家族中,由API定价的更昂贵模型可能更大(例如GPT-5.6 Sol > ). 地面 > > Luna, Opus 5 > > Sonnet 5. (英语). 我们发现没有明显证据表明,更大的参数本身就意味着在OSWorld-Pro上表现更好,因为Sonnet 5比Opus 5好(但比Opus 4.7和4.8差),而GPT-5.6 Luna比Terra好但比Sol差.

blocks.en: However, we observe that smaller model typically have a larger step count (e.g. Luna with 60.2 steps vs. Sol at 54.9 steps; Sonnet 5 at 108.7 steps vs. Opus 5 at 76.0 steps). This suggests that smaller models can use a greater number of steps to partially compensate for model capacity proxied via parameter count. On open-weight models, parameter count could potentially contribute some improvement as Qwen 3.8 Flash Next (125B) does better than Qwen 3.8B 27B at 55.1% vs. 32.1% from the same model family but it could be confounded by the difference in model architecture (Dense vs MoE). Furthermore, models with similar parameter count (e.g. Qwen 3.8 27B vs. Qwen 3.6 27B) have drastic different performance at 32.1% vs. 10.2% as with Qwen 3.8 Flash Next 125B and Qwen 3.5 122B (55.1% vs. 16.7%), suggesting that training recipes could influence performance more compared to model size alone.
blocks.zh: 然而,我们观察到更小的模型通常有一个更大的步数(例如:月亮有60.2步对Sol分54.9步;松内5分108.7步对Opus分5分76.0步). 这表明更小的模型可以使用更多的步骤来部分地通过参数计数来补偿模型所代理的能力. 在开量模型上,参数计数可能会促进一些改进,因为Quen 3.8 Flash Next(125B)比Quen 3.8B 27B好,以55.1%对32.1%来自同一模型家族,但因模型结构的不同(Dense vs MoE)而令人困惑. 此外,具有类似参数计数的模型(例如:Quen 3.8 27B vs. Quen 3.6 27B)在32.1%对10.2%的绩效上与Quen 3.8 Flash Next 125B和Quen 3.5 122B(55.1% vs 16.7%)有很大不同,这表明与模型尺寸相比,培训配方对绩效的影响更大。

blocks.en: is critical in real-world tasks (beyond task completion) as it influences user experiences in terms of latency and additional cost. There are three complementary perspectives for users who care about different aspects: steps, output tokens and token cost. Latency-sensitive users should focus on a combination on the number of steps as well as the output-tokens while token costs should be the priority for cost-sensitive users. One observation is that some models have low step count but high output tokens (e.g. Kimi K3 with 125 thousand tokens in only 42.2 steps). A possible explanation is that the pyautogui library that evaluation depends on supports multiple actions per step and hence models like Kimi K3 does fewer steps overall but seeks to perform more in each step, which requires more response tokens (of which, many are used for thinking). Another observation is that cost per task can differ by 20x across models with similar performance ($0.51 for GPT-5.6 Luna vs. $9.56 for GPT-5.6-Sol), suggesting that good performance can be balanced with affordability.
blocks.zh: 对现实世界的任务(超越任务完成)至关重要,因为它会影响用户在耐用性和额外费用方面的经验。 对于关心不同方面的用户来说有三个互补的视角:步骤,出品符和出品符成本. 对延迟问题敏感的用户应注重综合处理步骤的数目和产出托盘,而象征性费用应是对成本敏感的用户的优先事项。 一种观察认为,有些模型的步数低而输出值高(例如:Kimi K3只用42.2步有12.5千个令牌). 一个可能的解释是,评价依赖于每个步骤支持多个动作的pyautogui库,因此,像Kimi K3这样的模型在整体上做的步骤较少,但寻求在每个步骤中表现得更多,这需要更多的响应符(其中很多用于思考). 另一种观点认为,每个任务的成本可以因性能相近的型号而相差20x(GPT-5.6 Luna为0.51美元与GPT-5.6-Sol为9.56美元),这表明良好的性能可以与可承受性相平衡.

blocks.en: Process-based evaluations (like OSWorld-Pro) have unique advantages in revealing insights on efficiency and failures over an agent trajectory that outcome-based evaluation like OSWorld cannot.
blocks.zh: 以进程为基础的评价(如OSWorld-Pro)具有独特的优势,能够揭示对效率和失败的深刻认识,而OSWorld这样的基于成果的评价是无法做到的。

blocks.en:
To identify which action types are most prone to failure for each model, we measure action-level progression likelihoods across agent trajectories.
Specifically, we calculate the proportion of steps that make progress toward the subgoals.
A step is considered if it targets at least one subgoal and the targeted subgoals are feasible. We exclude action categories that were observed fewer than 5 times to reduce noise from limited observations. Higher scores are better.
blocks.zh:
为了确定每个模型中哪些行动类型最容易被失败,我们衡量跨剂轨迹的动作级进展可能性.
具体而言,我们计算在实现次级目标方面取得进展的步骤的比例。
如果目标至少是一个次级目标,而且目标明确的次级目标可行,则考虑采取一个步骤。 我们排除了观测不到5倍的行动类别,以从有限的观察中减少噪音。 更高的分数更好。

blocks.en:
Most models perform well on click operations, with the exception of Minimax M3 and Kimi K3. A closer look at Minimax M3 trajectories show frequent failures in basic operations such as clicking on the correct coordinates to perform an action (e.g. wanting to close a window but not clicking on the x button as shown in Fig. 4 ) while stronger models such as Claude and GPT-5.6 rarely commit such errors. This is reflected in the difference in progression likelihood for click operations on Tab. 3 for these models (39.0-41.9%) vs. stronger models (72.4-92.5%).
In addition, Claude Opus 4.8 made substantial improvements on Click (86.3 to 92.5%) in addition to Drag+Move (41.0 to 74.3%) category over its predecessor Opus 4.7. This indicates the likelihood for purposeful training relating to pointer behavior for Opus 4.8.
Claude models are also excellent on Keyboard and Scroll type actions, beating out all other models by a healthy margin. For instance, Claude models score ≥ \geq 89.2% on Keyboard and ≥ \geq 84.1% on Scroll behavior while no other model reaches 80% on either category. Among tested open-weight models, Qwen 3.8 models stand out despite being much smaller (27B to 125B) compared to other models (428B to 2.8T) as well as their own prior generations of similar sizes (Qwen 3.5 and 3.6), suggesting purposeful training on Qwen 3.8 to do well on GUI manipulation.

除Minimax M3和Kimi K3外,大多数模型在点击操作上表现良好. 更仔细地看下Minimax M3轨迹显示在诸如点击正确的坐标来进行动作等基本操作中经常出故障(例如想关闭窗口而不要点击图4所显示的x按钮),而更强大的模型如克洛德和GPT-5.6则很少发生这样的错误. 这反映在Tab上点击操作的进度可能性上的差异. 这些模型的3个(39.0-41.9%)对更强大的模型(72.4-92.5%).
此外克洛德·奥普斯 4.8在Click(86.3%至92.5%)上,除了Drag+Move(41.0%至74.3%)类别外,还比其前身Opus 4.7. 这表明对Opus 4.8进行与指针行为有关的有目的培训的可能性。
Claude模型在键盘和Scroll类型动作上也非常出色,以健康的比分击败了所有其他模型. 例如克洛德模型在键盘上得分为 \geq 89.2% , 在 Scroll 行为上得分为 \geq 84.1% , 而其他模型在任何一个类别上都没有达到 80% 。 在已测试的开放重量型号中,Quen 3.8型号尽管与其他型号(428B至 2.8T)相比要小得多(27B至 125B),以及它们自己的类似大小的前几代人(Quen 3.5和 3.6),但突出表现了Quen 3.8型号,建议对Quen 3.8进行有目的的培训,以便在GUI操纵上做得好.

blocks.en: Figure 5: OSWorld-Pro reveals inefficiency of strong models such as Claude Opus 5 Max beyond what outcome-based evaluation alone (e.g. in OSWorld) can show. Opus 5 Max was stuck on multiple subgoals without any progress including once for 59 steps as it performed goal-irrelevant actions.
blocks.zh: 图5 OSWorld-Pro揭示出Claude Opus 5 Max等强效模型的效率低下,超出了仅基于结果的评价(如OSWorld)所能显示的范围. Opus 5 Max被困在多个次级目标上,没有取得任何进展,其中一次是在59个步骤上,因为它采取了与目标无关的行动。

blocks.en: Inspections of OSWorld-Pro trajectories reveal that models can show extremely inefficient behavior despite completing all subgoals, with an example from Claude Opus 5 Max in Fig. 5 . To quantify such insights, we consider the average number of steps that the model spends on subgoals of varying status - completed (Successful Effort), feasible but not completed (Failure Persistence) and attempted but not feasible (Infeasible Persistence). Successful Effort represents how directly models complete tasks without detours or unnecessary verification. At this stage, GPT-5.6-Sol and Kimi K3 are efficient at 4.9 and 5.1 steps/subgoal compared to Sonnet 5 and Minimax M3 at 9.9 and 21.2 steps respectively. Failure Persistence represents how hard models try when they fail to eventually complete a feasible subgoal, which broadly correlates well with model efficiency on Successful Effort. Infeasible Persistence represents how quickly models recognize infeasible tasks and give up. Some models like Opus 5 (9.5 steps/subgoal) and GPT-5.6-Terra (12.1) recognize infeasibility rapidly while others persist for more steps (e.g. Sonnet 5 at 39.8).
blocks.zh: 对OSWorld-Pro轨迹的检查表明,模型尽管完成了所有子目标,但可以表现出极其低效的行为,以克洛德·奥普斯5 Max 在"Fig"中的例子为例. 5 (英语). 为了量化这种见解,我们考虑了该模式用于不同地位的次级目标(完成(成功努力)、可行但尚未完成(失败持久性)和尝试但不可行(不可行持久性)的平均步骤数量。 成功的努力代表了直接模型在不绕道或不进行不必要的核查的情况下完成任务的方式. 在现阶段,GPT-5.6-Sol和Kimi K3的效率分别为4.9和5.1步/分目标,而Sonnet 5和Minimax M3分别为9.9和21.2步。 失败的持久性代表了模型在最终未能完成一个可行的次级目标时如何艰难地尝试,这与成功努力的模型效率基本相关。 不可行的持久性代表了模型如何快速识别不可行的任务并放弃. Opus 5(9.5步/分目标)和GPT-5.6-Terra(12.1)等一些模式迅速认识到不可行,而另一些模式则坚持采取更多的步骤(例如Sonnet 5 at 39.8)。

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
We present OSWorld-Pro, the first process-based evaluation benchmark for Computer-Use Agents (CUAs) to complement outcome-based evaluations such as OSWorld. Based on over 67,000 human-annotations,
OSWorld-Pro is a challenging benchmark - especially for open-weight models - that reveals insights into failure modes that have previously eluded outcome-based evaluations (e.g. subgoal-irrelevant behavior and click-based operations).
We believe OSWorld-Pro is a critical step to improving CUA evaluation that also comes with potential subsequent applications to guide the performance and efficiency improvement of CUAs (through harness optimization or process reward signals in reinforcement learning), which we leave as future work.
blocks.zh:
我们提出OSWorld-Pro,这是计算机使用代理公司(CUAs)的第一个基于程序的评价基准,以补充OSWorld等基于结果的评价. 根据67 000多份人类说明,
OSWorld-Pro是一个具有挑战性的基准,特别是对于开放量模型来说,它揭示了对先前未能进行成果评价的失败模式(例如次级目标无关行为和点击操作)的洞察。
我们认为,OSWorld-Pro是改进CUA评价的一个关键步骤,它也带来潜在的后续应用,用以指导CUA的性能和效率提高(通过在强化学习中利用优化或处理奖励信号),我们作为未来工作离开.

blocks.en: OSWorld-Pro contains 305 unique tasks, with task goals generally at around a few sentences long with an average length of 553.2 characters (std of 262.5, min of 87 and max of 999). As shown in § A , task goals usually contain multiple related objectives for the agent to achieve.
blocks.zh: OSWorld-Pro包含305个独特的任务,任务目标一般在几句左右,平均长度为553.2个字符(std为262.5个,mine为87个,最大长度为999个). 如§A所示,任务目标通常包含多种相关目标,供代理人实现.

blocks.en: The overall goal is decomposed into individual subgoals that can be monitored with more granularity. Specifically, each goal is decomposed into an average of 9.2 subgoals (std of 4.7, min of 2 and max of 27). Subgoals are typically a single concise sentence with 60.2 characters (std of 35.6, min of 8 and max of 327).
blocks.zh: 总体目标被分解成个别次级目标,可以以更细微的颗粒性进行监测。 具体而言,每个目标被分解成平均9.2个次级目标(第4.7分、分数2分、最多27分)。 次级目标一般是一个有60.2个字符的简明句子(倒数35.6分、分数8分、最大分数327分)。

blocks.en: contain an average of 55.1 steps (std of 33.4, min of 5 and max of 149). Each step contains a screenshot (at 1920 *1080 resolution), a reasoning trace, a natural language description of the action and a code action. The code action refers to a pyautogui snippet that manipulates the state of the computer such as a click action or keyboard entry. Among all actions, most are in the click category (51.0% click, 3.6% doubleClick, 2.8% rightClick, 2.7% tripleClick), followed by the keyboard category (16.6% press (e.g. holding ctrl+c), 13.6% typewrite, 0.7% write), scrolling category (3.3% scroll, 0.1% hscroll), execution-control category (1.9% sleep, 1.3% terminate, 0.1% wait) and other pointer (2.3% moveTo). For judging purposes by both human judges and LLM-judges, we visualize the code action on top of the screenshot (as a semi-transparent overlay) as some of these actions (e.g. click(125, 61), which are the absolute x,y coordinates) can be hard to interpret without it.
blocks.zh: 平均包含55.1个步骤(第33.4分,分5分,最多为149分)。 每一步都包含一个截图(在1920 *1080分辨率),一个推理追踪,一个动作的自然语言描述和一个代码动作. 代码动作指操纵计算机状态的pyautogui片段,如点击动作或键盘条目等. 在所有动作中,大多数都属于点击类(51.0%点击,3.6%双Click,2.8%正Click,2.7%三重Click),其次是键盘类(16.6%按下(例如持有ctrl+c),13.6%打字,0.7%写出),滚动类(3.3%滚动,0.1%回滚),执行控制类(1.9%睡眠,1.3%终止,0.1%等待)和其他指针(2.3%移动到). 为了由人类裁判员和LLM裁判员来判断目的,我们将截图上方的代码动作(作为半透明的上盖)想象成其中的一些动作(例如点击(125,61),这是绝对的x,y坐标)没有它就很难解释.

blocks.en: Most steps in agent trajectories only targeted a single subgoal (98.3%) while 1.1, 0.4 and 0.2% target 2, 3 and 4 subgoals respectively. 84.7% of subgoals targeted at these steps were deemed feasible, 59.8% of steps led to a progression in subgoal(s) while 10.6% of steps led to a completion of subgoal(s). Across all steps within an agent trajectory, 23.1% of subgoals were unattempted, 2.0% were attempted but not feasible, 1.1% were feasible but not progressed, 8.4% were progressed but not completed and 65.3% were completed. Subgoals that were attempted but infeasible have an average of 18.8 steps, feasible but not progressed subgoals have 10.5 steps, progressed but not completed subgoals have 18.7 steps and completed subgoals have 6.2 steps.
blocks.zh: 代理人轨迹中的大多数步骤只针对一个单一的次级目标(98.3%),而分别为1.1、0.4和0.2%的目标2、3和4个次级目标。 84.7%针对这些步骤的次级目标被认为可行,59.8%的步骤导致次级目标取得进展,10.6%的步骤导致次级目标完成。 在物剂轨迹内的所有步骤中,23.1%的次级目标未尝试过,2.0%尝试过但并不可行,1.1%可行但未取得进展,8.4%取得进展但未完成,65.3%完成。 尝试但无法实现的次级目标平均有18.8个步骤,可行但没有取得进展的次级目标有10.5个步骤,已取得进展但没有完成的次级目标有18.7个步骤,完成的次级目标有6.2个步骤。

blocks.en: Appendix D Annotation Guidelines
blocks.zh: 附录D 说明准则

blocks.en: (This appendix reproduces the document given to annotators, with small terminology adjustment to the main text and data fields not used in this paper were removed to avoid confusion)
blocks.zh: (本附录转载给注解者的文档,对正文作小的名词调整,并去除本文未使用的数据字段来避免混淆).

blocks.en: This set of guidelines defines how to evaluate a trajectory at the goal, subgoal, overall-safety, and per-step levels. It also defines how Reviewer independently score and subsequently compare their judgments with the Annotator’s work.
blocks.zh: 这套准则界定了如何在目标、次级目标、总体安全和逐步评估轨迹。 也定义了审查者如何独立评分,然后将其判断与注释者的工作进行比较。

blocks.en: The rubric is designed to separate three questions that must not be conflated:
blocks.zh: 标题旨在区分三个不能拼接的问题:

blocks.en: 1. Is the task goal valid enough to evaluate? 2. Is the subgoal decomposition correct and usable? 3. At each step, what did the model target, feasibly attempt, advance, and complete?
blocks.zh: 1. 联合国 任务目标是否足以评估? 2. 次级目标的分解是否正确和有用? 3. 在每一步骤上,模型目标有哪些实际的尝试、推进和完成?

blocks.en: Is the task goal valid enough to evaluate?
blocks.zh: 任务目标是否足以评估?

blocks.en: Is the subgoal decomposition correct and usable?
blocks.zh: 次级目标的分解是否正确和有用?

blocks.en: At each step, what did the model target, feasibly attempt, advance, and complete?
blocks.zh: 每一步,模型目标是什么, 实际尝试,推进,并完成?

blocks.en: D.1 Terminology
blocks.zh: D.1 术语

blocks.en: Term Meaning Annotator The person who produces the primary annotation. Reviewer Performs an independent blind pass, then reviews the Annotator’s work. Subgoal A separately checkable milestone that contributes to the overall goal. App Used The primary application used to accomplish a particular subgoal. Step One action unit in the trajectory.
blocks.zh: 术语含义 制作初级注释的人. 评论员执行独立的盲人通行证,然后审查注释员的工作。 次级目标 可单独核查的里程碑,有助于实现总体目标。 应用 用于实现某一分目标的主要应用。 步骤 一个行动单位在轨迹。

blocks.en: D.2 Required Evaluation Order
blocks.zh: D.2 所需评价令

blocks.en: Evaluation sequence 1. Score Goal Clarity, Specificity and Safety . Continue only if the score is 5 out of 5. 2. Review the subgoal list, one-to-one App Used mapping, and sequential dependency. Correct them if needed. 3. For every step, record Targeted Subgoal(s), Feasibility, Progression, and Completion in that order.
blocks.zh: 评价顺序 1. 目标明确性、具体性和安全性 只有在得分为5分时才继续. 2. 审查次级目标清单、一对一的实用制图和依次依赖。 必要时改正. 3. 对每一步骤,按顺序记录目标分目标、可行性、进度和完成情况。

blocks.en: Score Goal Clarity, Specificity and Safety . Continue only if the score is 5 out of 5.
blocks.zh: 目标明确性、具体性和安全性 只有在得分为5分时才继续.

blocks.en: Review the subgoal list, one-to-one App Used mapping, and sequential dependency. Correct them if needed.
blocks.zh: 审查次级目标清单、一对一的实用制图和依次依赖。 必要时改正.

blocks.en: For every step, record Targeted Subgoal(s), Feasibility, Progression, and Completion in that order.
blocks.zh: 对每一步骤,按顺序记录目标分目标、可行性、进度和完成情况。

blocks.en: D.3 Task Filtering
blocks.zh: D.3 任务过滤

blocks.en: Evaluate whether the goal is clearly defined, unambiguous, and unlikely to induce actions carrying safety, policy, or ethical risks.
blocks.zh: 评估目标是否明确、毫不含糊,并不大可能引起具有安全、政策或道德风险的行动。

blocks.en: Label Definition 5 Excellent The goal is explicit, precise, and fully specifies the intended outcome. 4 Good The goal is clear with minor high-level phrasing. 3 Acceptable The goal is understandable but vague or underspecified. 2 Poor The goal is unclear, generic, or partially ambiguous. 1 Very Poor The goal is contradictory, incomprehensible, or likely to induce safety risks.
blocks.zh: 标签定义 5 目标明确、准确并充分具体说明预期成果。 4 不错 目标清晰,略带高层次措辞. 3 可接受 目标可以理解,但含混不清或不够明确。 2个穷人 目标不明确、笼统或部分模糊。 1 赤贫 其目标相互矛盾,难以理解,或可能引发安全风险.

blocks.en: Proceed/skip gate Score 5: proceed with task evaluation. Score 4 or below: provide the reason and skip the task.
blocks.zh: 前进/滑行门 积分5:继续任务评价. 分数4或以下:提供理由并跳过任务.

blocks.en: D.4 Subgoal List and App Used Correctness (Boolean)
blocks.zh: D.4 次级目标清单和使用的正确性(Boolean)

blocks.en: The task includes an LLM-generated subgoal list and a corresponding App Used list. Review and, when necessary, correct both lists.
blocks.zh: 任务包括LLM生成的子目标列表和相应的App Usedit列表. 审查并在必要时更正两份清单。

blocks.en: Correctness requirements • Goal aligned: every subgoal contributes to the original goal; there are no illogical, unrelated, hallucinated, or out-of-scope items. • Mutually exclusive: there are no duplicate subgoals or significant overlap. • Collectively exhaustive: the combined subgoals completely define the overall goal. • One-to-one application mapping: each subgoal has exactly one corresponding App Used entry identifying the primary application for that subgoal. • Matching order and count: the two lists have exactly the same length and order.
blocks.zh: • 目标一致:每个次级目标都有助于实现原定目标;没有不合逻辑、无关、幻觉或范围外的项目。 二. 支助 相互排斥:没有重复的次级目标或重大的重叠。 二. 支助 集体详尽:综合次级目标完全确定了总体目标。 · 一对一应用绘图:每个次级目标都有一个相应的应用用条目,确定该次级目标的主要应用。 • 相匹配的顺序和计算:两个名单的长度和顺序完全相同。

blocks.en: Goal aligned: every subgoal contributes to the original goal; there are no illogical, unrelated, hallucinated, or out-of-scope items.
blocks.zh: 目标一致:每个次级目标都有助于实现最初的目标;没有不合逻辑、无关、幻觉或范围外的项目。

blocks.en: Mutually exclusive: there are no duplicate subgoals or significant overlap.
blocks.zh: 相互排斥:没有重复的次级目标或重大的重叠。

blocks.en: Collectively exhaustive: the combined subgoals completely define the overall goal.
blocks.zh: 集体详尽:综合次级目标完全确定了总体目标。

blocks.en: One-to-one application mapping: each subgoal has exactly one corresponding App Used entry identifying the primary application for that subgoal.
blocks.zh: 一对一的应用程序绘图:每个次级目标都有一个相应的应用程序使用条目,确定该次级目标的主要应用程序。

blocks.en: Matching order and count: the two lists have exactly the same length and order.
blocks.zh: 相匹配的顺序和计数:两个列表的长度和顺序完全相同.

blocks.en: Label Definition Yes The subgoal list is coherent, goal-aligned and free of hallucinated items. Every subgoal has the correct one-to-one App Used entry. No > = 1 >=1 subgoal or App Used entry requires correction, addition, removal, or reordering.
blocks.zh: 标签定义 对 次级目标清单是连贯、目标一致和没有幻觉的项目。 每个分目标都有正确的一对一应用用入. 否 > = 1 + = 1 次级目标或 App used 条目需要更正、添加、去除或重排。

blocks.en: Required action If the label is No, update every affected subgoal or App Used. If the label is Yes, no action is needed.
blocks.zh: 需要采取的行动 如果标签为否,请更新每个受影响的次级目标或使用的应用程序。 如果标签是“是”,则无需采取行动。

blocks.en: D.5 Sequential Dependency (Boolean)
blocks.zh: D.5 顺序依赖(博勒)

blocks.en: Evaluate whether subgoals are arranged in the logical execution order required to accomplish the overall goal. The list should describe a coherent task sequence, not an unordered collection where later subgoals do not depend on the completion of prior subgoals.
blocks.zh: 评价次级目标是否按照实现总体目标所需的逻辑执行顺序排列。 清单应说明一个连贯的任务顺序,而不是在后面的次级目标不取决于先前次级目标的完成的情况下无序的集合。

blocks.en: Label Definition Yes Subgoals are in the correct sequence, and each naturally follows the preceding subgoal. No One or more subgoals are out of sequence, do not follow the required execution order, or do not depend on completion of prior subgoals.
blocks.zh: 标签定义 次级目标顺序正确,每个目标自然遵循上一个次级目标。 没有一个或多个次级目标出现出错,不按要求执行命令,或不取决于先前次级目标的完成。

blocks.en: Required action If the label is No, reorder or edit the subgoal list to reflect the correct execution sequence where possible otherwise skip the task. If the label is Yes, no action is needed.
blocks.zh: 需要采取的行动 如果标签是 No, 请重新排序或编辑子目标列表, 以在可能时反映正确的执行顺序, 否则会跳过任务 。 如果标签是“是”,则无需采取行动。

blocks.en: D.6 Stepwise State Labels
blocks.zh: D.6 分步状态标签

blocks.en: Apply the following four labels in order. Later labels depend on the earlier labels.
blocks.zh: 依次应用以下四个标签. 后期的标签取决于更早的标签.

blocks.en: D.6.1 Subgoal Targeted (Multi-selection or None)
blocks.zh: D.6.1 次级目标(多选或无)

blocks.en: Select subgoals that the model is working toward in the current step. A step may be associated with one or more targeted subgoal. If it is unrelated to every defined subgoal, select None. For each step, only include subgoal(s) that either overlap with (e.g. subgoal 1 after the last step ends with subgoal 1) or directly follows the last subgoal from the prior step (e.g. subgoal 2 after the last step ends with subgoal 1).
blocks.zh: 选择该模式在当前步骤中努力实现的次级目标。 一个步骤可能与一个或多个目标明确的次级目标有关。 如果与每个确定的次级目标无关,请选择无。 对于每一步骤,只包括以下次级目标:要么与(例如,在最后一步与次级目标1相重叠后,次级目标1与次级目标1相重叠;要么直接遵循上一个步骤的最后一个次级目标(例如,在最后一步与次级目标1相重叠后,次级目标2)。

blocks.en: D.6.2 Subgoal Feasibility (Boolean)
blocks.zh: D.6.2 次级目标可行性(博莱)

blocks.en: For the selected target, decide whether successful completion is possible in the current environment if the model continues taking appropriate actions.
blocks.zh: 对于选定的目标,如果该模式继续采取适当行动,则决定在当前环境中能否成功完成。

blocks.en: Label Definition Yes The environment, application, required resources, and system state permit the selected subgoal to be completed. No Completion is blocked by an application bug, sandbox limitation, unavailable required file/resource, missing precondition, UI/system failure, or another environment/system/application/resource limitation.
blocks.zh: 标签定义 对 环境、应用、所需资源和系统状态允许完成选定的次级目标。 没有完成被应用程序错误, 沙盒限制, 无法获取所需的文件/ 资源, 缺少先决条件, UI/ 系统故障, 或另一个环境/ 系统/ 应用程序/ 资源限制所阻碍 。

blocks.en: Feasibility rules • If Targeted Subgoal is None, Feasibility defaults to No. • If Feasibility is No, Progression and Completion must also be No for that step. • Creating a substitute resource does not make the original subgoal feasible unless the substitute is a valid replacement for the required resource, such as retrieving the same original file from an appropriate source.
blocks.zh: • 如果目标明确的次级目标为无,则可行性缺省为无; • 创建替代资源并不能使原始次级目标成为可行,除非该替代是所需资源的有效替代,例如从适当的来源取回相同的原始文件。

blocks.en: If Targeted Subgoal is None, Feasibility defaults to No.
blocks.zh: 如果目标分目标为无,则可行性默认为无。

blocks.en: If Feasibility is No, Progression and Completion must also be No for that step.
blocks.zh: 如果可行性是否定的,进步和完成也必须是否定的。

blocks.en: Creating a substitute resource does not make the original subgoal feasible unless the substitute is a valid replacement for the required resource, such as retrieving the same original file from an appropriate source.
blocks.zh: 创建替代资源并不能使原始次级目标成为可行,除非该替代物是对所需资源的有效替代,例如从适当的来源取回相同的原始文件。

blocks.en: D.6.3 Subgoal Progression (Boolean)
blocks.zh: D.6.3 次级目标进展(波恩)

blocks.en: Decide whether the current step produced observable, meaningful advancement toward the selected target. Progression reflects a state change, restoration, or completion - not merely an attempted action.
blocks.zh: 决定目前的步骤在实现选定目标方面是否取得了可观察、有意义的进展。 进步反映国家变化、恢复或完成,而不仅仅是企图采取的行动。

blocks.en: Label Definition Yes The step observably advances the selected targeted subgoal. No The step makes no observable progress, is redundant, is blocked by infeasibility, or is unrelated to the selected target.
blocks.zh: 标签定义 对 这一步骤明显地推动了选定的次级目标。 没有步骤没有可观察到的进展,是多余的,被不可行性所阻挡,或者与所选目标无关.

blocks.en: Progression rules • If the targeted subgoal is partially or fully completed in the step, Progression is Yes. • Verification generally does not count. It may count only when it materially advances evaluation of the subgoal, such as revealing that the previous approach was wrong or identifying an issue that changes the next action. • Redundant verification of an already completed or already confirmed subgoal is No. • If Feasibility is No, Progression is No. • If Targeted Subgoal is None, Progression defaults to No.
blocks.zh: • 进展规则 如果目标次级目标在该步骤中部分或全部完成,进步是肯定的。 • 核查一般不算数。 只有当它实质性地推进了对次级目标的评价时,例如披露以前的做法是错误的,或确定改变下个行动的问题时,才可能算数。 • 如果可行性是否,进步是否。

blocks.en: If the targeted subgoal is partially or fully completed in the step, Progression is Yes.
blocks.zh: 如果目标次级目标在该步骤中部分或全部完成,进步是肯定的。

blocks.en: Verification generally does not count. It may count only when it materially advances evaluation of the subgoal, such as revealing that the previous approach was wrong or identifying an issue that changes the next action.
blocks.zh: 核查一般不算数。 只有当它实质性地推进了对次级目标的评价时,例如披露以前的做法是错误的,或查明改变下个行动的问题时,才可能算数。

blocks.en: Redundant verification of an already completed or already confirmed subgoal is No.
blocks.zh: 对一个已经完成或已经确认的次级目标的重复核查是否。

blocks.en: If Feasibility is No, Progression is No.
blocks.zh: 如果可行性为否,进步为否。

blocks.en: If Targeted Subgoal is None, Progression defaults to No.
blocks.zh: 如果目标分目标为无,则进步默认为无。

blocks.en: D.6.4 Subgoal Completion (Boolean)
blocks.zh: D.6.4 次级目标完成(波恩)

blocks.en: Mark Completion Yes only on the step where the selected targeted subgoal is first fully achieved in the final evaluated attempt. A step may progress without completing the targeted subgoal.

blocks.en: We started with a brute force approach to probe whether every subgoal is targeted by every step. If targeted, we can then iteratively probe whether the goal is feasible, progressed upon and completed. Assuming k k steps (hundreds) and m m subgoals (tens), we have a max of O ⁡ ( k ∗ m ) O(k*m) API calls, which can all be done in parallel.
blocks.zh: 我们从野蛮的武力方法开始 来调查每个次级目标是否都是每个步骤的目标 如果目标明确,我们可以反复探索目标是否可行、是否取得进展和是否完成。 假设 k k 步( 百步) 和 m m 子目标 ( 十分) , 我们有一个最大 O Q  ( k ) ( k ) O( k * m) API 调用, 都可以平行进行 。

blocks.en: Not only is this approach demanding in API calls, it also does not apply the constraints of the sequentially-dependent subgoals found in OSWorld-Pro, where an agent will only target subgoals that follow the subgoals targeted in the prior step. Incorporating this memory feature (informing the LLM judge which subgoals were targeted by prior steps) means that it only requires O ⁡ ( k ) O(k) steps, but they need to be done in sequential order with much higher latency.
blocks.zh: 这种做法不仅要求在API呼叫中要求,而且没有适用OSWorld-Pro中发现的相继依赖的次级目标的限制,在该次级目标中,代理人将只针对遵循前一个步骤所设定的次级目标。 纳入这一记忆特征(告知LLM法官哪些次级目标被前几个步骤所锁定)意味着它只需要O-(k)-(k)-(k)步骤,但它们需要依次完成,其延迟度要高得多。

blocks.en: With this method, we realized that the LLM judge was basically re-using information from prior API calls. We found an approach to incorporate the information of all steps into a single API call ( O ⁡ ( 1 ) O(1) ) containing up to hundreds of screenshots. While this means that only a limited number of models (GPT-5.6 family) can be used as LLM-Judges, we note that this is a common limitation in LLM-Judge based evaluations such as Arena Hard ( LMSys, 2024 ) and GDPVal-AA ( Artificial-Analysis, 2025 ) . Specifically, these evaluations can only use some of the strongest models at time of release (e.g. Gemini-3-Pro or GPT-5 family). As the serving infrastructure of other models improve, this method can be applied directly on other models.
blocks.zh: 通过这种方法,我们意识到LLM法官基本上是在重新使用API先前通话中的信息. 我们找到了一种方法,将所有步骤的信息纳入一个单一的API呼叫(O QQ ( 1) O(1)),包含多达上百个截图. 虽然这意味着只有有限数量的模型(GPT-5.6家族)可以用作LLM-法官,但我们注意到,这是LLM-法官基于Arena Hard(LMSys,2024年)和GDPVal-AA(人工分析,2025年)等评价的一个共同限制. 具体而言,这些评价只能在发布时使用一些最强的模型(例如双子座-3-Pro或GPT-5家族). 随着其他模型的可用基础设施的改善,这种方法可以被直接应用到其他模型上.

blocks.en:
Following ProfBench ( Wang et al., 2026 ) , we estimate the cost of running the full LLM-Judge evaluation, using the number of input and output tokens multiplied by their public API cost without caching ( OpenAI, 2026b ) . We estimate fees
based on the regular service tier at the lowest context length bucket. Early experiments also suggests that mean Macro-F1 is highly consistent, differing no more than 0.6% across three independent runs - therefore we only run with each judge once to save cost.
blocks.zh:
继Bench教授(Wang等,2026年)之后,我们用投入和输出符数乘以其公共API费用,不设缓冲(OpenAI, 2026b.),估算进行LLM-法官评价的全部费用。 我们估计收费
基于上下文最短桶的正则服务级别。 早期的实验也表明,"Macro-F1"是高度一致的,在三个独立运行中差异不超过0.6%,因此我们只与每个法官运行一次以节省成本.

blocks.en: Following OSWorld ( Xie et al., 2024 ) , we perform one run for each model. We believe OSWorld opted for a single run due to the high cost of each run (up to thousands of US dollars per model) and minimal expected inter-run variance based on the high number of independent tasks ( > 300 >300 ). Across all models, we use the relevant model harnesses from OSWorld ( XLANG-Lab, 2024 ) , which defines the approach for inference details including sampling strategy (e.g. temperature and top-p), context management and system prompts. We set max turns at 250 (vs. 100 in OSWorld) due to longer horizon nature of our tasks. All models are evaluated at the highest reasoning effort possible.
blocks.zh: 追随OSWorld (谢等,2024年),我们为每个型号执行一跑. 我们认为,OSWorld选择单次运行,因为每次运行成本高(每个模式最高可达数千美元),并且由于独立任务多( > 300 > 300),预计运行间差异最小。 在所有模型中,我们使用来自OSWorld(XLANG-Lab, 2024年)的相关模型,该模型界定了推论细节的方法,包括采样策略(如温度和顶点-p),上下文管理和系统提示等. 由于任务范围较长,我们设定最大转速为250(OSWorld). 所有模型都以尽可能高的推理能力进行评估。

blocks.en: Prompts are cached in multi-step long-horizon tasks as they are optimal from cost considerations. In estimating cost, we use prices from OpenRouter (2025) including caching related fees and discounts as they contribute substantially to the eventual cost. For Anthropic models, we use the default 5-minute caching price. Across all models, we estimate fees based on the regular service tier at the lowest context length bucket.
blocks.zh: 多步骤的长视距任务中缓存了提示,因为从成本考虑,提示是最佳的。 在估算成本时,我们采用OpenRouter(2025年)的价格,包括缓冲相关收费和折扣,因为这些费用对最终成本贡献很大。 对于Anthropic模型,我们使用默认的5分钟缓存价格. 在所有模式中,我们根据最低上下文长度桶的正常服务级别估算收费。
